rationale: Y's finding #1 (default sleep() level=2 permanently bricks the engine after wake_up, since the NotImplementedError guard fires on the common bare-sleep() path) is a precise, high-value hit on the latent gap — it matches almost exactly the real regression (#4905/#4912) that the human review missed, with a concrete actionable fix (change default to level=1). Y also engages the ground-truth 'enum for sleeping tags' concern directly (finding #5), which X never addresses. X contributes one genuinely valuable unique catch (global vs per-stage _sleeping_tags bug) and solid CI-coverage findings, but its two near-duplicate, externally-unverifiable docs findings hurt precision, and its handling of the level-2 restriction stays framed as a docs-sync issue rather than questioning the guard's strictness for existing callers. Both are highly actionable with file/line evidence.
